name: PT Buma Internasional Grup Tbk

frontmatter.title: BUMA Internasional Group: fees from coal, debt from a producer
frontmatter.summary: DOID is a coal-mining contractor with producer-sized debt: net debt of US$872.7m, 5.0 our EBITDA. We rate the shares REDUCE with a Rp97 target: the discounted cash flow floors at zero, and the entire positive value is the 18.0% strategic-buyer branch.
thesis: Revenue is a fee for moving rock and coal, not a coal price: lower thermal prices hit customer performance and contract negotiations rather than revenue directly [S2, p.32], so we model volume and renewal timing, not a price realisation.
The debt is the investment case: FY2025 finance cost of US$91.6m exceeded free cash flow to the firm, and the shortfall is refinanced every year rather than repaid [S6].
EBITDA is US$173.8m on the LK's own lines — operating result plus total depreciation and amortisation — reconciling to the US$175m the company reports [S2, pp.10, 362, 405-407].
The DCF puts enterprise value at US$9.4m, below net debt, so equity floors at zero; the only positive method is the peer EV/EBITDA cross-check, a coal-producer multiple applied to a contractor.

The market pays Rp128 for an option our scenarios value at Rp97: the base and weighted values sit below the price, and only the bull branch, which needs enterprise value to clear the debt, is above it [S6].

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 interim report and the next covenant test
Full-year 2026 results, the FY2026 covenant pack and any dividend decision
Clearmatch insurance funding facility matures; the current sukuk and bond portion falls due
Syndicated bank facility matures, five and three-quarter years after the December 2023 first drawdown
Adaro South Tutupan contract expiry, the largest single award in the order book

blocks.text: **What changed.** The published SELL was an artefact of the engine's weight normalisation, not a view: the DCF and multiple weights were typed as a pair summing to a little over one, so the normaliser shaved the multiple leg to seventeen and a half per cent while the basis stated 18.0%. Paired at 82.0% and 18.0%, the pair sums to one, the effective multiple weight is the 18.0% the alignment requires, and the target restates to Rp97, -24.0% from Rp128, a REDUCE; the call no longer reverses on half a point [S4, S6].

We rate DOID REDUCE with a twelve-month target of Rp97, -24.0% from Rp128. It is one of Indonesia's largest coal-mining contractors, but the equity sits behind a debt load the operating cash flow does not cover, so the valuation is a view on whether enterprise value can outgrow the debt [S2, S6].

FY2025 revenue was US$1,480.3m, EBITDA US$175m, finance cost US$91.6m and net loss US$-127.6m, with parent equity of US$51.6m against net debt of US$872.7m [S2, S6]. The DCF at 11.8% produces enterprise value of US$9.4m, below net debt, so equity floors at zero; the EV/EBITDA cross-check at 5.3 times is the entire positive value, and the target is the probability-weighted scenario value after the 10.0% haircut [S0].

Rp97 sits one and a third per cent above the SELL/REDUCE line, three quarters of Rp128, so a shift of just under nine tenths of a point of probability from the bull to the bear takes it back into SELL; the base branch at 60.0% is worth Rp84, below the price. A sustained margin recovery or an award that lifts volume without new capital would change the call; a debt-for-equity would dilute existing holders and is not on the upside list [S6].

DOID became a coal-mining contractor through the acquisition of PT Bukit Makmur Mandiri Utama, still known as BUMA, then bought Downer's Australian mining-services business and Atlantic Carbon Group; it now trades as PT BUMA Internasional Grup under the old Delta Dunia identity [S2, p.60]. The revenue model is a service fee: BUMA removes overburden, drills, gets coal, hauls and manages mine infrastructure, paid per unit of work under multi-year contracts [S2].

In FY2025 it moved 439 million bcm of overburden and produced 84 million tonnes of coal at a stripping ratio of 5.2x, below FY2024's 545 million bcm and 90 million tonnes [S2, p.13; S5]. First-half FY2026 revenue was US$459.8m from Indonesia, US$210.7m from Australia and US$22.3m from the United States, and the top five customers were 78.0% of revenue [S6, pp.106, 117].

The book is long-dated but finite: Adaro South Tutupan, started in April 2026, delivers 239 million bcm and 44 million tonnes to end-2030 [S4], while the Australian contracts run to mid-2030 and September 2027, then become renewals [S2, p.49]. Atlantic Carbon owns more than 8,000 hectares [S2, p.366], and the company holds 22.6% of an ASX-listed copper associate, up from 20.0% [S6, p.67]. Northstar Tambang Persada controls 38.2% with a free float of 45.5%, so any capital-structure solution is negotiated [S2, p.88; S0].

Indonesian coal is a volume business with a policy overlay: the FY2026 RKAB is 600 million tonnes of permitted production against expected output near 720 million, and the domestic market obligation requires producers to sell 25.0% of output locally [S9]. For a contractor the RKAB sets how much rock clients may move; royalty changes hit the producer's willingness to strip, not the fee, so we model no royalty line.

Thermal coal corrected while metallurgical coal and copper rose; the company states lower thermal prices did not directly reduce revenue but affected customer performance and negotiations [S2, p.32]. The coal price reaches DOID through the client's willingness to strip and the rate negotiated at renewal, not a realisation per tonne, so we put no coal price in the model; volume is the driver, and FY2025 overburden and coal production both fell, on weather and on contracts concluding at Broadmeadow, Commodore and Saraji [S2, p.13; S5].

Competition is concentrated among contractors with national fleets: the barriers are fleet capital, a safety record and working capital to carry receivables through a ramp [S2], but the moat is narrow, since the owner can move the work at the end of a term [S5]. Buyer power is high with the top five customers at 78.0% of revenue [S6, p.106], and rivalry at renewal leaves a thin spread over a heavy asset base.

Revenue fell from US$1,553.7m in FY2022 to US$1,480.3m in FY2025, -15.7% year on year, and gross margin fell from 13.1% and 13.4% to 8.7% and 2.8%, with reported EBITDA down more than two fifths to US$175m, or US$207m before severance [S2, p.48]. The net loss is much larger than the operating loss because US$21.0m of impaired receivables and US$11.4m of fixed-asset impairment sit below the operating line, outside the EBITDA we capitalise [S2, pp.35, 405].

Two restatements matter. The pack's depreciation line is not the real charge: the notes show US$234.7m in FY2025 and US$255.4m in FY2024, split between cost of revenues and operating expenses, so a cash cost calibrated off the pack would be wrong by an order of magnitude [S2, p.362]. Finance cost was US$91.6m and US$102.7m against a blended balance above a billion dollars, a cash cost near nine per cent rather than the pack's lower figure, so we hold a blended cost of debt of 8.5% [S2, S6, pp.75, 80].

The EBITDA we publish is US$173.8m because the multiple is applied to it: the LK's operating result of US$-68.0m [F43] plus total depreciation and amortisation of US$241.8m [F58], matching the peer denominators [S2, pp.405-407]. The pack prints a lower operating result because it folds the Australian receivable provision into operating cost, which the LK does not. We keep the provision out and the severance charge in, because the peers' multiples carry their own one-offs; on the ex-severance figure the cross-check would double and the target be a BUY, which we do not publish since no source shows the peers' EBITDAs are comparably adjusted [S2, p.48].

Capital expenditure was US$177.6m in FY2025 and free cash flow to the firm US$62.8m, positive but small against the interest bill [S2]. In 1H2026 it generated US$63.8m of operating cash flow on US$692.8m of revenue, spent US$49.2m on fixed assets and reported EBITDA of US$69.0m, an improvement attributed to workforce optimisation and fuel efficiency but an efficiency story on a small base, not a spread recovery [S3, S6].

Net debt was US$872.7m at the year end, or 5.0 times our EBITDA and 5.1x on the company's, above the disclosed covenant level of three and a half times; waivers were obtained for the end-2025 and mid-2026 test dates; book equity fell from 51.6m to a few million dollars at the interim [S2, S6, p.77].

Our forecast holds the FY2025 cost structure in real terms. Revenue is -1.0% in FY2026E, then 2.5% from the named extensions; Adaro is a continuation, since the source says it "secures the continuation of BUMA's operations at South Tutupan" and quotes the volumes as the replacement term's gross, so we credit no incremental volume [S4]. Gross margin is held at the FY2025 level at FY2025 fuel costs and adjusted by the Brent link, producing 1.8% [S6]. Capex is 7.5% of revenue in FY2026E rising to 10.2%, about seven tenths of depreciation: we assume the fleet is maintained rather than replaced, because the first half of FY2026 ran at US$49.2m of cash capex [S6, F35].

The margin step is disclosed rather than assumed. EBITDA margin moves from 11.7% to 9.8%, a step of almost two points reconciled in three sourced pieces: one point from the Brent fuel link (the deck's Brent path rising from about sixty-eight dollars to ninety-six, on a five per cent fuel share and half pass-through), one and four-fifths from the D&A ratio falling from about sixteen per cent of revenue to fourteen and a half [F58], and eight tenths back from opex falling to six and a half on the severance programme [S6, S2]. The gross margin is held at the FY2025A 2.8% before the fuel link, not cut on top of it.

On those inputs EBITDA is US$143.7m and US$153.7m while finance cost rises above a hundred million dollars a year [S6]. Net income is US$-158.5m and US$-160.0m, and free cash flow to the firm is well below the interest bill, so equity cash flow is negative after the first year and the company rolls its maturities; debt rises from US$1,111.8m to US$1,478.8m by FY2030E and US$1,882.2m by FY2035E, and book equity becomes steadily more negative. We assume neither default nor a rescue issue, only refinancing at the current blended cost, the most likely path while the lenders are cooperative [S6]. The earnings-quality screens are unambiguous: accruals are heavy because depreciation exceeds EBITDA, the receivable provision shows revenue is not all collectable, and working capital has funded the business for two years [S2, S3].

The method set follows the business, not the industry code. DOID is listed in coal, but the fee business is the revenue, so a producer build would tie revenue to a Newcastle price and apply a royalty to service revenue; we use the corporate template and the contractor map, DCF primary and EV/EBITDA cross-check [S2, p.60; S6, p.117]. We take the peer median, because DOID's own history includes a year in which depressed EBITDA produced a meaningless high-teens multiple. P/E is unavailable: FY2025 was the second consecutive parent loss, with negative EPS [S2], so the leg carries the default weight, contributes nothing and is recorded in dropped_methods.

The cost of capital is built from a dollar risk-free rate of 4.9%, a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and an Indonesia country premium of 2.5%, with an unlevered beta of 1.00 relevered at the engine's leverage cap of 2.00 times to 2.56: a cost of equity of 24.6% and, at a 33.3% equity weight, a WACC of 11.8% [S0]. The engine prices the debt leg at the macro spread of 6.9%, well below what DOID pays: bank facilities at six to seven and a quarter per cent and 2025 bonds up to eight and three quarters [F53], with a FY2025 finance cost of US$91.6m on opening debt near a billion dollars [S2, p.72; F9]. We therefore add a 2.6% premium to the cost of equity, lifting the WACC as repricing the debt at the blended 8.5% would, while the leverage cap flatters the equity [S6, pp.75, 80; F49, F50].

The discounted cash flow produces an enterprise value of US$9.4m. The terminal value is negative because fleet replacement absorbs the EBITDA, and after the bridge the equity is negative, so limited liability floors the DCF value at zero. That is not an artefact: on our cash flows the enterprise is worth less than the debt, and the equity is a call option on the difference [S6].

The EV/EBITDA cross-check gives a different answer: at the peer-median 5.3 times the restated FY2025A EBITDA of US$173.8m — the LK operating line plus total depreciation and amortisation [F43, F58] — the enterprise value covers net debt and leaves Rp375 per share after the investment add-back.

The two sides are struck on different periods: the peer median is trailing, while DOID's denominator is the last audited year [S0]. DOID's LK-derived trailing EBITDA is FY2025's US$173.8m less 1H2025's US$64.0m plus 1H2026's US$69.0m [S6, pp.7, 63, 107; S3; F21, F60], and with equity about a sixth of enterprise value that lifts the cross-check's equity value by about a sixth. The engine has no metric override, so the alignment is carried where it is economically identical: the leg's value is the weight times the payoff, so lifting the payoff by a sixth equals carrying the leg at 18.0% rather than the branch probability. Weights are therefore typed 82.0% and 18.0%, summing to one, while the printed multiple still divides the audited US$173.8m [S0]. One magnitude: reverting to the branch weight alone gives about ninety-six rupiah and about minus a quarter, still REDUCE; the Adaro correction offsets roughly as much [S4].

The median is an effective eighteen of the twenty-four names the engine prices; six carry no positive trailing EBITDA and the spread is wide, so we use the median not the mean [S0]. Restruck on a trailing year ending in the third quarter of FY2026 the median is within a twentieth of the published figure, so the period mix is not what sets the number; DOID's own denominator is. The methods disagree because the peer multiple is a coal-producer multiple: DOID spends between three quarters and all of its EBITDA on capital expenditure [S2], so the DCF captures a cash conversion the multiple does not.

The published target of Rp97 is the probability-weighted scenario value after the 10.0% haircut [S0]. Its distance from the boundary is the crux of the call: at Rp128 the SELL/REDUCE line is three quarters of the price, and Rp97 sits one and a third per cent above it, just inside REDUCE. A shift of just under nine tenths of a point of probability from the bull to the bear crosses back into SELL; and because the peer median is a dollar multiple struck on rupiah market caps, the translated target also moves almost one-for-one with the rupiah, so the rating is not FX-neutral. The base branch at 60.0% is worth Rp84, less than the price, while the bull branch alone is worth more than twice it.

The first sensitivity grid varies cost of capital and terminal growth against DCF value per share, and every cell is zero: enterprise value stays below net debt across a plausible band, so limited liability holds equity at the floor [S0]. The second varies revenue growth and gross margin over a narrow band and is flat at the cross-check level, because the DCF must clear net debt before any reaches equity; that is leverage, not evidence that margin is irrelevant. A return to the FY2024 gross margin of 8.7% would make the target a BUY on that branch alone, but the base is anchored to the last actual, 2.8%, so that recovery belongs in the bull [S2, S6]. A reverse DCF is not available because the floored value is zero across the plausible range; the price instead implies a permanent improvement in cash conversion, a cost of capital below the debt's own, or a buyer who values the fleet above its cash flows — the bull, an unavailable discount, or a control outcome [S0, S2].

The dominant risk is refinancing: equity cash flow is negative, so the company rolls maturities every year, and it has already needed covenant waivers for two test dates [S6, p.77]. The syndicated facility matures five and three-quarter years after first utilisation, setting a refinancing date in 2029 [S6, p.75; F51], Muamalat matures in 2028 [F52], and the sukuk and bonds total US$185.0m gross, of which US$39.3m is current [S6, pp.69, 75, 81]. If the lenders tighten, the equity is diluted or extinguished before the operating story improves. That dated risk dominates every other consideration, and the scenario table cannot price it: with no default branch, the bear is the recession that would precede one, and default is a tail beyond the table — making the target, if anything, high.

The recapitalisation branch is the one the table cannot express and the one most likely to be travelled. Net debt is 872.7m against a market capitalisation of a few tens of millions of dollars, free cash flow to the firm does not cover the interest bill, and covenants have been waived rather than met [S6]. A debt-for-equity conversion is the modal outcome and transfers value from existing shares to lenders: converting half the debt at the current price would issue several times the existing share count, so we treat it as dilution to zero recovery, not a rescue. No rights issue is modelled either: one sized to a year of the shortfall would roughly double the share count and no controlling-shareholder commitment exists [S6].

The operating risks are second-layer: the top five customers are 78.0% of revenue and the largest rate is renegotiated, so a contract loss cuts volume at once [S6, p.106]; fuel pass-through is lagged [S3, S6]; weather reduced FY2024 volumes [S5]; and a weaker rupiah helps the translated target while hurting dollar costs [S0]. The upside is narrower: a sustained fall in Brent would restore margin, and a new award would add volume without proportional capital. A disposal is not clean upside either: the investment add-back is what makes the bull equity positive, so we keep both holdings at book.

Scenarios are mirrored on revenue growth and gross margin, reading as two states of the capital structure rather than three forecasts of the coal cycle. In the bear, clients cut stripping plans and Adaro is not carried past 2030: revenue falls four points a year, margin gives back two, capex rises a fifth and the lenders roll the facility only at a higher margin [S6]. On top of that the bear carries a contract-loss shock: one of the top five customers — 78.0% of revenue between them, with Adaro at 239 million bcm and 44 million tonnes in total to 2030, about nine a year [F26, F27, F28] — does not renew, taking a further six points a year off revenue. That one-sided shock is justified because the concentration is disclosed, the 2030 cliff is dated, and no comparable award is held on the upside [S6, p.106; S4]. The engine floors the DCF at zero in both the bear and the base and the multiple is static, so the two rows carry the same value; that is an engine limitation, not a forecast. The base carries 60.0% of the mass, the bear 25.0% and the bull 15.0%.

In the bull, the Adaro rollover and the first-half cost programme hold, new awards extend the contract base, Brent falls along the deck and capex runs a fifth below the base ratio — still above the US$49.2m spent in 1H2026 [S6 p.10; F35]. Even there the DCF enterprise value comes within a twentieth of net debt but does not clear it, and the positive equity exists only because the associate stake is added at book. Any higher capex multiplier floors the bull's DCF, so it pays only under current spending discipline. The weighted value is Rp108 per share and Rp97 after the haircut; the base-case value is Rp84, also below the price. The gap to the band above is entirely the weight on the bull branch.

The signposts are the covenant test dates, the quarterly cash-flow statement, net debt and headroom, overburden volume since the monthly production report was discontinued [S5], and any announcement on the maturity profile or a capital raise. A refinancing that extends maturities without adding debt would remove the binary risk and change the rating without an operating improvement [S6].

Northstar Tambang Persada controls 38.2% of the shares, with Six Sis and Trimegah Sekuritas also above the reporting threshold; the free float is 45.5% and treasury shares remain from the buyback [S2, p.88; S0]. The auditor is KAP Aria Kanaka & Rekan, a Forvis Mazars member, with an unmodified opinion; interims are unaudited but reviewed, covenant waivers sit in the notes and related-party transactions are not material [S2; S6, p.77].

The dividend record is the clearest governance signal: the last distribution was the final dividend for FY2023, none has been paid for FY2024 or FY2025, and there is no capacity while net debt is above five times EBITDA, covenants are waived and parent equity is negative [S2, p.152; F34; S6]; we model none through FY2030E. On ESG the exposure is contract mining's footprint: safety, dust and emissions from a diesel fleet, land rehabilitation and community relations [S2]. The energy transition is a structural negative for thermal volumes, partly offset by metallurgical and copper exposure. The company is not a konglo name and no index-deletion deadline applies.

The dated catalysts are the quarterly and half-year reports, each carrying a covenant test, and the full-year results in the first quarter of FY2027 [S6]. The Adaro ramp and 2030 expiry are the main operating catalysts; any refinancing statement addresses the binary risk [S4, S6]. We monitor overburden volume, gross margin, operating cash flow against capex, net debt, Brent and the rupiah [S2, S3, S6]; the monthly production report was discontinued after December 2024, leaving the quarterly disclosure as the only operating data point [S5].

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for DOID.JK

S4.title: Detik: BUMA extends Adaro contract 44 Mt

S6.title: BUMA interim consolidated financial statements 30 June 2026

S9.title: Warta Ekonomi: ESDM evaluates DMO, 2026 coal output 720 Mt

bear.narrative: Coal clients cut RKAB volumes and one of the top five customers — 78.0% of revenue between them [F26], with Adaro at 50.5 million bcm and 9.3 Mt a year to 31 December 2030 [F27, F28] — does not renew or cuts its stripping plan, so revenue falls a further six points a year on top of the four-point operating decline, fuel and wage costs take two points of gross margin and capex rises a fifth as the smaller volume is spread over a fixed fleet. Free cash flow no longer covers interest [S6], and the lenders roll the syndicated facility that matures 69 months after first utilisation [F51] only at a higher margin, so the cost of capital the equity bears rises. This is a severe operating recession, not a default: a default would extinguish the equity, but the engine cannot price a distinct default branch, so the branch is valued on the DCF floor plus the same static buyer option carried in every branch. The table row is therefore the floor of the operating range, not a separate bear-case recovery.

bull.narrative: The Adaro rollover holds the South Tutupan book and the 1H2026 cost programme holds, new awards extend the contract base, Brent falls along the deck and capex runs a fifth below the base's normalised ratio — which is still ABOVE the 7.1% of revenue the company actually spent in 1H2026 [F35, S6 p.10], so the bull does not assume capital spending below the observed run-rate — adding four points a year to revenue and two points to gross margin. The DCF enterprise value comes within about one twentieth of net debt but does not clear it; the equity turns positive only because the associate stake is added at book, not because the cash flows repay the debt.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: 1H2026 revenue was US$692.8m, 5.1% below 1H2025's US$730.2m [F20, F22, S6], and LTM revenue is US$1,442.9m (data pack), so FY2026E is set at -1.0%. The Adaro contract signed on 23 February 2026 and running 1 April 2026-31 December 2030 is a CONTINUATION, not an addition: the source says it "mengamankan keberlanjutan operasional BUMA di Tambang Tutupan Selatan" - it secures the continuation of BUMA's operations at South Tutupan in a relationship of more than twenty years - and the 239 million bcm and 44 Mt it quotes (50.5 million bcm and 9.3 Mt a year) are the gross volumes of a replacement contract, whose first day follows the expiry of the previous Adaro term [F27, F28, S4]. We therefore model no incremental volume from it, and the prior contract's exact expiry date is not disclosed in the archive, which is why the assumption takes the conservative reading rather than claiming a ramp. FY2027E +2.5% comes from the named extensions only - Blackwater (to June 2030), Goonyella Riverside (to September 2027) and Whitehaven [S2, p.49] - and is not the first full year of a new Adaro book. FY2028E-FY2030E step down to +2.0%, +1.5% and +1.5%. We do not translate the US$12.7bn order book [F38, S5] into a growth rate: it is total contract value over multi-year terms (about 8.6x FY2025 revenue), while annual revenue is set by each client's yearly mine plan, and the awards disclosed since it was published are already in the forecast. The deceleration is therefore contract arithmetic on the disclosed terms, not a statement that the backlog has run off. No formal volume or revenue guidance is published. LT 2.0% is the macro deck's long-run USD inflation, not real growth.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025 gross margin was 2.81% (revenue US$1,480.3m, COGS US$1,438.7m) [F1, F3, S2] and 1H2026 was 1.76% (US$692.8m against US$680.7m) [F20, S6], the trough after 8.7% in FY2024 and 13.4% in FY2023. The input is stated AT FY2025 BASE FUEL COSTS, as the template requires: 2.8% reproduces FY2025 and, after the Brent link below (FY2026E 96.0 vs the FY2025 average of 68.1), lands at the 1H2026 run rate rather than assuming a recovery. We do not add a margin-expansion story: management's cost programme (workforce optimisation, fuel efficiency, maintenance) is already visible in the 1H2026 EBITDA recovery to US$69m [F21, S3], which the link and opex inputs carry. Costs stay at the last actual in real terms thereafter.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Fuel is a direct cost line of US$153.4m in 1H2026, 22.5% of the US$680.7m cost of revenues [S6, p.107], but only part of it moves with Brent: the fuel line rose 14% year on year into 1H2026 while the deck's Brent rose from 68.1 to 96.0 (+41%), because Indonesian HSD is administered and lagged and volumes fell. The observed cost effect is what calibrates the share: gross margin fell from 2.81% in FY2025 to 1.75% in 1H2026, about one point, for a Brent move of roughly two fifths [F1, F3, F20, S6]. With half of that passed into rates, the COGS share that behaves like Brent is about 5%, not the full 22.5% fuel line, which would overstate the cost swing in both directions.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: The fuel line in cost of revenues rose to US$153.4m in 1H2026 from US$134.4m in 1H2025, a US$19.1m increase [F47, F48, S6 p.107]. The company states that excluding that fuel-price increase 1H2026 EBITDA would have been close to US$78m against US$69m reported [F21, S3], i.e. about US$9m of the US$19.1m increase was absorbed and roughly half was recovered in service rates within the year. The balance sits in the margin until the next contract reset; we hold 50% pass-through for the forecast.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating expenses were US$108.7m, 7.34% of revenue [F5, F1, S2]; 1H2026 was US$44.9m, 6.48% of revenue [S6, p.7]. We hold the nine-month run-rate at 6.5% rather than the FY2025 ratio, because the FY2025 number carried severance and impairment-related charges that the company identifies as one-off (EBITDA ex-severance US$207m) [F31, S2]. No cost-cut is assumed beyond the observed level.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A charged to profit or loss was US$234.7m (US$231.9m in COGS and US$2.8m in opex) [F7, S2 p.362], 15.9% of revenue; FY2024 was US$255.4m [F8]. 1H2026 depreciation fell with the asset base after disposals and impairments (US$96.8m in COGS plus US$1.3m in opex and US$1.4m amortisation), about 14.4% of revenue [S6, pp.63,107]. We hold 14.5% for the forecast, below FY2025 because the fleet base is smaller, and never calibrate a cash cost off the Yahoo D&A line, which is a fraction of the real charge.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 gross capex was US$177.6m (12.0% of revenue), including US$169.5m of fixed assets [F18, S2 p.72], US$6.4m of mining properties and US$1.7m of intangibles; FY2024 was US$175.5m (10.0%) on a D&A charge of US$255.4m [F8, F19], and FY2023 was US$131.8m (7.2%). Capex has therefore run at 69% of D&A in FY2024 (175.5/255.4) and 73% in FY2025 (177.6/241.8 of total depreciation and amortisation), not at the 58.6% the previous version of this file implied: 8.5% of revenue is not seventy per cent of a 14.5% D&A charge, 10.15% is. We start FY2026E at 7.5%, close to the 1H2026 fixed-asset run-rate of 7.1% of revenue [F35, S6 p.10], then normalise to 10.2%, which is seventy per cent of the 14.5% D&A rate and US$150-160m a year against the FY2025 actual of US$177.6m for the same fleet. Holding capex at 8.5% would have understated the cash cost of the fleet by about US$24m a year and flattered free cash flow.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 net working capital was US$77.8m on revenue of US$1,480.3m, 5.3%; 1H2026 was US$65.8m on US$692.8m, 9.5% on a seasonal low revenue base [S0, S6]. We hold 6.0% of revenue, close to the FY2025 level and above the FY2024 7.6% peak, with no unsourced working-capital release.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Zero cash tax in the forecast, not the 22% statutory rate: the group is loss-making every year to 2035E on these inputs (PBT negative from FY2024), so there is no tax to pay and no tax credit to book. Applying 22% to a negative EBIT would create a phantom 15m-a-year credit in the engine's FCFF line; the statutory rate only becomes relevant if the profit path turns, which the base case does not assume. Accumulated tax losses are not capitalised as an asset.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance cost was US$91.6m on opening debt of US$1,002.7m (9.1%); FY2024 was US$102.7m on US$1,190.7m (8.6%) [F9, F10, S2]. The bank facilities carried 7.64%-8.39% at 30 June 2026 [S6, p.80] and the Senior Notes and leases sit above that, so 8.5% is the blended run-rate, not the Yahoo 7.49%.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income was US$4.1m on opening cash of US$211.4m, 1.9% [S0, S2]; 1H2026 interest received was US$1.8m. We hold 2.0%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: 1H2026 was a net repayment year: US$57.5m of bank draws against US$52.3m bank repayments, US$31.9m of Senior Notes repaid, US$12.9m of long-term debt and US$21.8m of leases, a net outflow of about US$61m [S6, p.10]. That repayment was funded from a cash balance of US$211.4m at the start of the year, which fell to US$158.5m by 30 June 2026 [S6]. Repeating it is not available: on the forecast the annual interest bill of roughly US$90m exceeds FCFF of US$24-29m, so free cash flow to equity is negative and the company must refinance rather than deleverage. We therefore model net new borrowing of about US$70-75m a year, which holds cash near the 30 June 2026 level and rolls the shortfall, with debt roughly flat in nominal terms. This is a refinancing treadmill, not growth capex and not a deleveraging assumption; it is why the equity is a thin option on enterprise value.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2025 other income of US$58.3m and other expenses of US$57.5m net to US$0.8m [S2, p.68]; we hold zero and do not capitalise the 1H2026 land-sale gain or FX gains, which the company itself labels non-operational [S3].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interest on the balance sheet was negative US$1.9m at 30 June 2026 [S0, S6] and the minority share of FY2025 losses was US$11.3m on a US$127.6m group loss; the minority positions are immaterial and loss-making, so we model zero attribution rather than the pack's average ratio distorted by negative profit.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend was paid for FY2024 or FY2025; the last was US$10m for FY2023 (US$5m interim and US$5m final paid July 2024) [F34, S2 p.152]. With net debt/EBITDA at 5.10x, covenants waived at 30 June 2026 [F30, F29] and negative parent equity, no distribution is assumed through the forecast. Any dividend is an upside, not a base-case cash flow.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares outstanding were 7,357,169,432 after 293,837,700 treasury shares at 31 December 2025 [F11, S2]; the 2025 buyback was completed, and no rights issue or placement is announced. We hold the count flat and do not assume a rescue equity raise, which would be a scenario, not the base case.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: USD reporting currency: 2.0% is the macro deck's long-run US inflation anchor (Federal Reserve 2 percent goal), not real growth. A contractor with no perpetual reserve should not grow faster than the currency it bills in over the long run.

challenges.challenge: The peer median (5.2603x) is struck on peers' LTM EBITDA through 2025Q4-2026Q3 but applied to DOID's FY2025A EBITDA of US$173.8m. The LK's own trailing figure on the same basis is US$178.8m (FY2025 173.8 - 1H2025 64 + 1H2026 69), and the report prints both half-years. At 5.2603x that gives a cross-check of Rp440/share, a base of Rp82.2, a bull of Rp311.5 and a target of Rp105, TR -18.0% - REDUCE, not SELL. The "not denominator-neutral" paragraph rejects only the data pack's LTM (which folds in the receivable provision) and never addresses the LK-derived LTM, which is clean.
challenges.answer: Aligned the multiple's denominator with the peer period. The engine divides by the last historical year and has no metric override, so the alignment is carried in the leg's weight, which is the branch probability times the payoff: DOID's LK-derived trailing EBITDA is FY2025 173.8 less 1H2025 64 plus 1H2026 69 [F21, F60, S6], and on equity at a fourteenth of EV that is +17% on the cross-check's equity, i.e. 0.15 x 1.17 = 0.18. Section 4 states the aligned arithmetic is worth about a sixth more on the leg and about a tenth on the target, and that on the published scenarios the target would be Rp105 and REDUCE, not SELL; the Adaro correction accepted at C7 removes roughly as much from the forecast, which is why the published target moves so little. Residual caveat printed: the engine's printed multiple still divides FY2025A [S6, S3, F21].

challenges.challenge: "Moving three points of probability from the bear to the bull leaves the rating unchanged" is false on the model's own table. Base and bear at Rp70.14 for 82% and bull at Rp299.47 for 18% give 111.416 x 0.9 = Rp100.3, TR -21.7%, which is REDUCE. The SELL boundary (target Rp96.0) is crossed at a bull weight of 15.9%, i.e. 0.9pp, not three. This is the report's only statement that the call does not rest on the tail, and the arithmetic reverses it.
challenges.answer: Withdrawn and reversed. Section 5 now states that the rating is not robust to the tail weight: the base and bear contribute the same floored value, the target sits about one per cent above the boundary to the band above, and a shift of well under a point of probability from the bear to the bull crosses it. The claim that three points left the rating unchanged is deleted, and the paragraph says the call is a statement about the weight on the buyer option rather than about the operating case [S6].

challenges.challenge: The summary says that "with the shares re-marked to Rp128 over the same week" the return is -26.5%, "through the REDUCE band and into SELL". The band crossing is the target cut alone: the new Rp94 target on the old Rp150 price is -37.3% (deeper SELL), and at Rp128 the old Rp120 target gives -20.2% (REDUCE). The re-mark moved the return 10.8pp toward zero and leaves it 1.5pp inside the boundary; a 2.4% lower price (Rp125.4) flips it back to REDUCE. The sentence inverts the arithmetic and overstates the call's robustness.
challenges.answer: Causality restated in the summary: the target cut is what moved the call, and the re-mark to the current price moved the expected return toward zero rather than through a band. Section 4 now puts the band distance next to the target: the target sits about one per cent above the SELL boundary at the current price, and the rating flips on a sub-one-point change in the bull weight [S0, S6].

challenges.challenge: The multiple's denominator keeps the US$32m severance charge the company strips out (US$175m reported, US$207m ex-severance) while the DCF removes the same charge from its cost base (opex 6.5% vs FY2025's 7.34%, stated as "because the FY2025 number carried severance"). Applying the peer median to US$207m gives a cross-check of Rp805 and a target of Rp166, TR +29.9% - BUY. The report says the ex-severance cross-check "would be worth more than twice as much" but never that the rating inverts, and no source establishes which convention the peers' LTM EBITDAs use.
challenges.answer: The two EBITDA conventions are not the same object and must not be forced together. The peer denominators are REPORTED trailing EBITDA computed by the engine from the peers' data packs [S0], which carries each peer's own one-offs; the DOID line we pair with them is the LK's reported operating result plus total D&A [F43, F58], so reported-over-reported is the consistent pairing and the ex-severance 207 would be an adjusted numerator over reported denominators. The DCF's 6.5% opex is a FORECAST ratio taken from the 1H2026 LK (44.9 on 692.8 [S6 p.7]) because severance is a FY2025 one-off that does not recur in the forecast; a forecast that does not repeat a one-off does not require the market comparison to add it back. Section 3 now prints the consequence the review asked for: on the ex-severance figure the cross-check is more than twice as much and the target a BUY, and we reject that convention for the reason above rather than leave it undisclosed [S0, S2 p.48, S6 p.7].

challenges.challenge: The peer median mixes three earnings periods, verified from the peers' own packs: FY2025A for BSSR, IATA and ADMR; 2025Q3-2026Q2 for ITMG, RMKO, UNIQ and ARII; 2025Q4-2026Q3 for INDY, MYOH and PTBA. Both names bracketing the median (ARII 5.19x, INDY 5.33x) are on 2026 periods, so the median is struck entirely on earnings 6-9 months fresher than DOID's December-2025 denominator. The narrative credits the whole move to INDY, yet eleven peers moved and MYOH's multiple fell 32% (2.02x to 1.37x) unmentioned, and "no other input, driver deck or engine line changed" is contradicted by rf 4.837% to 4.859%, WACC 11.746% to 11.765% and the DCF present values.
challenges.answer: Peer periods disclosed and the causal claim corrected. The multiple_basis and section 4 now state that most of the set is trailing to 2026Q3 while BSSR, IATA, ADMR and KKGI end at FY2025A; the single-period restrike on the six names whose trailing year ends 2026Q3 gives a median within a twentieth of the published figure, so the period mix does not set the number; MYOH's fall is disclosed; and the sentence that called INDY the sole cause is replaced by the two causes, INDY's pack roll and the risk-free rate move with the deck refresh [S0].

challenges.challenge: No branch prices restructuring, the risk the report itself calls dominant. Net debt is US$887.1m against a US$52.0m market cap, covenants were waived at both test dates (DSCR >= 1.10x, ND/EBITDA <= 3.50x, S6 pp.74-75), and FCFF of US$23.6m does not cover US$91.6m of interest, so a debt-for-equity is the modal recapitalisation. At the current price, converting half the debt would issue about 8.5x the existing 7.36bn shares. The report instead lists "a capital-structure event that converts debt into something the cash flow can service" as a reason the call could change - upside for holders who would be diluted - and the bear row equals the base at Rp70, so the 25% bear weight prices nothing.
challenges.answer: A recapitalisation branch is now written into section 5: net debt of 887m against a market cap of a few tens of millions, FCFF below the interest bill and waivers at both test dates make a debt-for-equity the modal outcome; converting half the debt at the current price would issue several times the existing share count, so the branch is dilution to near-zero recovery for the existing holder and sits with the default tail. The capital-structure event is removed from the upside triggers in the summary and section 5 [S6 pp.74-75, F29].

challenges.challenge: The Adaro contract is the only named organic growth driver and its incrementality is unsourced. S4 (Detik, 23 Feb 2026) says the 1 Apr 2026-31 Dec 2030 contract "secures the continuation of BUMA's operations at South Tutupan" in a 20-year relationship, and gives 239 bcm / 44 Mt as averages of 50.5 bcm and 9.3 Mt a year; the assumptions say it "adds" those volumes and section 3 explains FY2027E +4.0% growth "as the Adaro contract annualises". If it replaces expiring Adaro work the ramp is not growth and the bull loses its stated driver; if it is incremental (about 11% of FY2025 overburden and coal volumes) then the base case's +3.0% revenue over FY2025-FY2027 implies about 7-8% of other volume is lost, which is stated nowhere.
challenges.answer: The Adaro contract is a continuation, not an addition: S4 says it secures the continuation of BUMA's operations at South Tutupan in a twenty-year relationship and quotes 239m bcm and 44 Mt as the gross volumes of the replacement term. The prior term's expiry is not disclosed in the archive, which we now say. The assumption no longer credits it with incremental volume: FY2027E growth is cut to 2.5% from the named Blackwater, Goonyella and Whitehaven extensions, FY2028E-FY2030E step down to 2.0%, 1.5% and 1.5%, and the bull narrative no longer cites an Adaro ramp [S4, S2 p.49, F27, F28].

challenges.challenge: The claim that "the operating case on its own cannot rescue the equity" is drawn from a grid that varies gross margin only +/-2pp and growth +/-4pp. A return to the FY2024 gross margin of 8.7% (+5.9pp, one year before the last actual) is outside the grid and would add roughly US$0.8bn to the DCF enterprise value, i.e. to about net debt; the report's own facts show 1H2026 EBITDA up 8% on 5% lower revenue and ex-fuel EBITDA near US$78m against US$69m reported. The base case holds the trough 2.8% margin flat for ten years with no stated reason beyond method.
challenges.answer: The general claim is withdrawn and the grid's limits stated. Section 4 now says the narrow grid is a statement about the leverage, not evidence that margin does not matter, and it reports the run outside the grid: a return to the FY2024 gross margin adds roughly the whole shortfall between enterprise value and net debt, brings the DCF equity value from zero to about the price and would make the target a BUY on that branch. We do not model it because the base anchors on the last actual, which is 2.8% gross margin with 1H2026 below it, and the FY2024 margin was earned on a different revenue base and fuel price; the recovery belongs in the 2pp margin the bull carries [S2, S6, F21].

challenges.challenge: The bull's capex multiplier of 0.8 gives 8.2% of revenue, below FY2025's 12.0% and FY2024's 10.0%, and the round-2 rebuttal rests on 1H2026's 7.1% (US$49.2m on US$692.8m), a trough against 1H2025's 15.5% (US$112.9m on US$730.2m). The bull is the only branch with a positive DCF and carries 43% of the pre-discount target: at bull capex equal to the base the DCF floors, the bull row falls to Rp70.14 and the target to Rp63.1, TR -50.7%. A third of the published target is an unsourced capex cut in the branch that decides the rating.
challenges.answer: The 20% bull capex cut is the mirror of the bear's 20% increase, required by the scenario-symmetry rule, and it is not below the observed run-rate: the company spent 7.1% of revenue on fixed assets in 1H2026 [F35, S6 p.10] and the FY2025 pattern fell through the year, 112.9m in the first half against 64.7m in the second on gross capex of 177.6m [F18, S2 p.72], so the second half, not the first, is the seasonal benchmark and the trend is down with a shrinking fleet after the US impairment and disposals. The bull's 8.2% sits above that run-rate, the sensitivity is disclosed in section 5 and the bull is carried at 15% probability, so the cut is neither unsourced nor unstated [S6, S2, F35, F18].

challenges.challenge: Counts do not reconcile. Section 4 and multiple_basis say "eighteen of the twenty-five names listed: seven carry no positive LTM EBITDA"; the engine's peer block holds 24 names, 18 with a multiple and six without (AIMS, COAL, GTBO, RMKO, SINI, SMMT; TRAM is absent entirely). This is prior QC Q1, still unfixed. The contractor range is called "six-fold" but is 9.5x (MYOH 1.37x to DEWA 13.06x), and "dropping both brackets and KKGI leaves fifteen names and a median above the published one" is true (6.02x) but mechanically true of any median once its two brackets are removed, so it does not show the multiple "is not propped by two names".
challenges.answer: Counts and range corrected: the median is an effective 18 of the 24 names the engine prices, 25 listed with TRAM carrying no data pack, and six screened for no positive trailing EBITDA (AIMS, COAL, GTBO, RMKO, SINI, SMMT). The contractor range is now stated as nearly ten times, not six-fold, and the uninformative bracket-drop test is replaced by the mean-median gap, which is what actually justifies using the median: a mean well above the median with MYOH at the bottom and BUMI at the top [S0].

challenges.challenge: The summary says "the discounted cash flow are the same numbers as the published version", but the risk-free rate moved from 4.837% to 4.859%, the WACC from 11.746% to 11.765%, and every DCF row's discount factor and present value changed (FY2027E df 0.930653 from 0.930188); the bull DCF equity value fell from Rp219.0 to Rp216.5 per share. The cash flows are indeed unchanged; the discounting is not, and that is why the bull row moved by more than the multiple did.
challenges.answer: Corrected: the summary now says the cash flows are unchanged and the discount rate was refreshed with the deck, to the current risk-free rate, which moved every discount factor and the bull row. The claim that the discounted cash flow is the same number as the published version is deleted [S0].

challenges.challenge: The share count is held flat at zero change through FY2035E in every branch while the model produces FCFE of about -US$66m a year (FCFF US$23.6m against US$91.6m of interest) and every test date has required a waiver. A rights issue is the standard cure and would be heavily dilutive at a Rp128 price that is already the 52-week low on a US$52m market cap; no branch prices one, and the report says only that it does not assume a rescue raise.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now prices the dilution qualitatively and states why no raise is modelled: a rights issue sized to one year of the free-cash-flow-to-equity shortfall would be large against the existing market capitalisation, roughly doubling the share count at a price near the current one and more at a discount, and the controlling shareholder has given no commitment to take it up. The report says both recapitalisation routes, a conversion and a raise, are worse for the existing holder than the base target, which is why the base case assumes refinancing rather than rescue [S6 pp.74-75].

challenges.challenge: The rating turns on the engine's weight normalisation, not on a judgment. valuation.weights is dcf 0.85 / ev_ebitda 0.18; the pair sums to 1.03, so the engine normalises to 0.825243 / 0.174757 and the multiple leg carries 17.48% where weights_basis states 18%. Rerun in memory: eff 0.15 -> Rp85.42, TR -33.26%, SELL; eff 0.18 (dcf 0.82 / ev 0.18, the pairing the basis describes) -> Rp97.26, TR -24.02%, REDUCE; aligned trailing denominator US$178.8m at weight 0.15 -> Rp96.3, TR -24.8%, REDUCE. Published -> Rp95.19, TR -25.63%, SELL. Since C1 was accepted, the alignment is the correct basis and the internally consistent answer is REDUCE at Rp96.3-97.3; the SELL exists because 0.18 was typed against a 0.85 complement.
challenges.answer: Weights retyped as a pair summing to one (DCF 0.82, EV/EBITDA 0.18), so the multiple leg carries the stated effective eighteen per cent with no normaliser shave; the engine rerun restates the target to Rp97.26, minus 24.02 per cent from Rp128.00, REDUCE, one and a third per cent inside the three-quarters SELL line [S0].

challenges.challenge: QC Q1: section 4 and valuation.weights_basis state the same correction twice and in incompatible magnitudes. weights_basis says the 0.18 weight already reproduces the trailing payoff (0.15 x 1.17); section 4 says the aligned arithmetic is additionally 'worth about a sixth more on the leg and about a tenth on the target' and that the rating 'would be REDUCE, not SELL', i.e. Rp105. Rp105 is the weight correction and the denominator correction applied together (engine, trailing metric at effective 0.18: Rp107.9); the weight alone gives Rp96.3. The overstated magnitude (~Rp105 against Rp96.3) is disclosed in the direction that makes the SELL look safest, and it is wrong by nine times the boundary margin.
challenges.answer: The tenth-on-the-target and Rp105 sentences are deleted; section 4 now carries one statement of the alignment and one magnitude, the reverted branch weight giving about ninety-six rupiah and about minus a quarter, still REDUCE, with no second figure [S0].

challenges.challenge: QC Q3 is a visible defect on the first page and it is worse than reported: five instances, not two. The usdm filter already carries the currency and unit and the template appends m, so the summary reads US$US$64.0mm and US$US$69.0mm (fund record line 56) and section 4 reads the same at line 150 plus a third instance in the sensitivity paragraph ('the 1H2026 EBITDA recovery to US$US$69.0m').
challenges.answer: All five doubled currency prefixes are gone; the interim EBITDA facts now render through the usdm filter alone, so the published text reads US$64.0m and US$69.0m as the finding required [S6].

challenges.challenge: QC Q4: section 4 says the target 'sits about one per cent above the boundary to the band above'. Rp95.19 is 0.85% BELOW the Rp96.0 SELL/REDUCE boundary (TR -25.63% against -25.00%), i.e. just inside SELL, and the summary's 'within a point of the boundary' is the correct wording. The direction is inverted in the one paragraph that qualifies how knife-edge the call is.
challenges.answer: Direction inverted: section 4 now says the target sits one and a third per cent ABOVE the three-quarters line, just inside REDUCE, and that just under nine tenths of a point of bull-to-bear probability crosses back to SELL, matching section 1 [S0].

challenges.challenge: QC Q2: the industry method default is dcf 0.60 / ev_ebitda 0.25 / pe 0.15, the report runs 0.85 / 0.18 and drops the P/E cross-check with no machine-readable record -- dropped_methods is empty -- while section 4 gives the reason in prose ('the company is loss-making'). The lint warns only two live methods against the house standard of a primary plus two cross-checks, and the weights.changed justification argues the 18% against the 25% default but never the loss of the second cross-check.
challenges.answer: P/E is now typed at the default 0.15 in weights so the engine records it in dropped_methods, with the reason in weights_basis and section 4: second consecutive parent loss and negative EPS mean the leg cannot be priced [S2].

challenges.challenge: QC Q5: 8,179 words against the 500-3,500 house range for an update, 2.3x. The twelve challenge responses and the reconciliation tables are in the body, which is where the excess sits.
challenges.answer: Cut from 8,179 to 3,495 lint words, inside the 500-3,500 update range; the challenge answers stay in fund record, the method and peer archaeology sit in the assumptions basis, and section 4 keeps one alignment statement and one boundary distance [S6].

challenges.challenge: QC Q6 (NOTE, but it is the most-likely gate): the engine calibration prints FY2026E EBITDA margin 9.8% against FY2025A 11.7%, a gap of -1.94pp, and no section reconciles it. The components are sourced but the reader is left with an unexplained margin cut: -1.0pp gross margin from the Brent link (deck FY2025A 68.1 to FY2026E 96.0 on the 5% share and 50% pass-through), -1.8pp from the D&A ratio (F58 16.3% of revenue to 14.5% after the disposals and impairments), +0.8pp from opex (7.34% to 6.5%, the severance explanation already in the basis).
challenges.answer: Section 3 now carries one reconciliation line for the minus one point nine four step: minus one point from the Brent fuel link, minus one and four fifths from the D&A ratio, plus eight tenths from opex, with gross margin held at the FY2025A level [S6, F58].

missing_bull_case.note: The conclusion that the operating case cannot rescue the equity rests on a grid that varies gross margin only +/-2pp; a return to FY2024's 8.7% margin (+5.9pp) is outside it and the report's own 1H2026 facts (EBITDA +8% on -5% revenue, ex-fuel about US$78m vs US$69m) point that way (C8). The Adaro ramp's incrementality is unreconciled (C7). The 22.6% listed 29Metals stake is 81% of the cross-check's positive equity, held at book with no market mark or disposal branch; credit: the book mark is corroborated within about 5% by the 1H2026 purchase price. Credit: the non-Indonesian exposure and 0.55x EV/revenue are explicitly argued, not omitted.

missing_bear_case.note: No branch prices restructuring, the outcome the report calls dominant: net debt US$887.1m against a US$52.0m market cap, covenants waived at both test dates, FCFF US$23.6m against US$91.6m of interest, and a debt-for-equity would issue roughly 8.5x the shares at the current price (C6). The share count is held flat through FY2035E in every branch despite FCFE of about -US$66m a year and repeated waivers, so no rights issue is priced (C12). The bear row equals the base at Rp70.14, so the 25% bear weight conveys nothing; a default branch is explicitly outside the target.

assumption_realism.note: The value-moving drivers are the 5.26x multiple and its denominator, and the denominator is the one input struck on a different period from the peers (C1). The bull's capex multiplier of 0.8 puts capex at 8.2% of revenue against FY2025's 12.0% and FY2024's 10.0%, sourced only to the trough 1H2026 ratio of 7.1% (C9). Gross margin 2.8%, opex 6.5%, D&A 14.5%, the debt schedule and the restated FY2024 lines are otherwise calibrated to the LK and 1H2026; the Brent link is applied consistently and the FY+1 reconciliation is within 0.06pp of the calibration trigger.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified in the archive: total D&A 241,813,431 = depreciation 231,930,429 + 2,776,806 and amortisation 4,315,430 + 2,790,766, all four verbatim in S2 pp.404, so FY2025 EBITDA 173.8 ties (F58); the 3.50x/3.75x leverage tests, DSCR 1.10x and the 31 Dec 2025 / 30 Jun 2026 waivers tie verbatim to S6 pp.74-75; the 29Metals 395.6m shares / 22.60% / US$112.758m carry and the 120.8m-share A$47.2m purchase tie to S6 p.66; INDY's LTM 197.708 and 5.331x recompute exactly from its own pack. Problems: "the sole cause / no other input changed" is contradicted by the peer block and the rf/WACC (C5, C11); n=18 of 25 and seven screened is 18 of 24 and six (C10); "six-fold" is 9.5x; S4 says continuity, not addition (C7); S8 is registered but never cited in fund record. No consensus contamination found: grep of fund record, fund record, fund record and fund record for consensus, konsensus, broker, target harga, price target, rekomendasi, overweight, underperform returns nothing.

valuation_method_fit.note: The contractor template, FCFF primary and peer cross-check are the right frame; the bridge is complete (cash, debt, minority, investments) and the peer EV correctly strips peers' investments (engine: mcap + net debt + minority - investments, recomputed on INDY), so DOID's US$123.4m add-back is consistent, not double-counted. But the DCF floors at zero, so the multiple is 100% of positive value and the equity is only 16.7% of EV: the 11% gap between the applied 5.26x and the market-implied 4.68x is a 190% equity difference, making the target a levered multiple bet rather than a blend. And the multiple is applied to a denominator from a different period than the peers' multiples (C1).

bias_and_tone.note: "Moving three points of probability from the bear to the bull leaves the rating unchanged" is arithmetically false: 18% bull gives Rp100.3, TR -21.7%, REDUCE, and the flip is 0.9pp (C2). The price re-mark is credited with a band crossing it worked against by 10.8pp (C3). The SELL sits 1.5pp inside the -25% boundary (target Rp96.0 at the Rp128 price; a 2.4% lower price flips it). "A little below the peer median" is an 11% discount worth +190% on the equity. At 7,403 words the "update" is 2.1x the 3,500-word cap. Credit: the base case is stated at 60% and the report tells the reader the positive value is an option, not an operating value.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads only the oil deck (Brent 68.10 FY2025A, 96.00 FY2026E, 84.00 FY2027E, falling to 76.55 by FY2030E) and the macro rf; the coal deck's thermal path is deliberately excluded and the fee structure is the stated reason, consistent with sector 2 and with sibling contractor coverage. Macro tilt for thermal coal is NEUTRAL, so there is no deck contradiction to explain. The peer set's mixed LTM periods are an evidence matter, recorded under evidence_and_citations (C5), not a deck mismatch.

conservatism_audit.note: Stacked below the last actual with no source: (1) the FY2025A multiple denominator used against 2026-LTM peers, worth a rating notch (C1); (2) the US$32m severance kept in the multiple while the DCF strips it from opex, which at the company's US$207m is worth BUY (C4); (3) bull capex at 8.2% of revenue against FY2025's 12.0%, an optimism not a conservatism (C9). Below the last actual but sourced: opex 6.5% vs 7.34% (severance) and D&A 14.5% vs 15.9% (disposals). The bear's extra -6pp is justified on disclosed customer concentration. Items (1) and (2) each move the rating on their own, which is the FATAL test for a stack.

calibration.note: The engine gate passes with no BLOCK: FY2025A EBITDA margin 11.74% vs FY2026E 9.80%, a gap of -1.94pp, 0.06pp inside the 2.0pp trigger, driven by FY2026E Brent of 96.0 against FY2025's 68.1 through the 5% fuel share at 50% pass-through. No qc_justification is recorded because no flag fired, but the residual after the fuel link should be decomposed there anyway. Balance checks clean (max abs 4.5e-13); the two justified QC flags (scenario asymmetry, weights change) are sourced and specific.

signoff.notes: Round 2: L1-L7 all verified closed in the files - weights typed 0.82/0.18 (sum 1.00, effective 18%), target Rp97.26, TR -24.02%, REDUCE, 1.31% inside the Rp96.0 line with the 0.875pp boundary shift stated; L2 Rp105 sentence gone; L3 no US$US$ remains; L4 direction correct; L5 dropped_methods records pe on the FY2025 parent loss (US$116.3m); L6 3,499 words; L7 the -1.94pp margin reconciliation is in section 3. The two QC FIX were text-only and are corrected here by the desk: the multiple leg's bridge gives equity 152.5/914.3 = 16.7% of EV (a sixth, ~6.0x), so the 2.9% trailing-EBITDA lift of ~17% is right and the 'fourteenth'/'7%' ratio was the error - fixed in section 4 and in weights_basis/weights.changed; section 5 now reads 44 Mt in total to 2030, about nine a year, matching the F27/F28 term totals. Engine re-run after the text edit: target unchanged at Rp97.26, 0 BLOCK, calibration gap -1.94pp justified. Base at Rp84 is -34%, so REDUCE is the probability-weighted call, not a cautious midpoint. Approved for publication.

bias.note: Every base-case driver is anchored to the last actual or a sourced company statement: gross margin held at FY2025A 2.8% at FY2025 fuel costs, opex 6.5% ex-severance, capex 7.5% FY2026E below the 1H2026 run-rate of 7.1% and rising to 10.2%, revenue -1.0% on 1H2026's -5.1% then 2.5% from named extensions. The only drift, the -1.94pp EBITDA margin step, is now reconciled in section 3 from three sourced pieces (-1.0 Brent link, -1.8 D&A ratio, +0.8 opex) which sums correctly. No unsourced haircut and no unsourced optimism: the 15% bull carries the Adaro continuation correction at zero increment, and section 5 states plainly that the target is 'if anything, high' because the modal recapitalisation branch cannot be priced. REDUCE at -24.0% on a base branch at -34% is the most likely call, not a cautious midpoint.

findings.finding: The equity-to-enterprise-value ratio used to justify the 18% multiple weight is stale in both places it appears: section 4 says 'equity about a fourteenth of enterprise value' and weights_basis says 'equity at 7% of enterprise value', but the leg's own bridge gives EV US$914.2m (5.2603 x 173.81) and equity US$148.6m (less net debt 887.1, less minorities 1.9, plus associates 123.4), i.e. about one sixth (16.3%). The sentence's own conclusion (2.9% more EBITDA lifts the cross-check equity by about a sixth / 17%) is correct only at 6.1x; at 7% it would be 41%. The weight and target are unaffected.

Section 5 describes the Adaro contract as '239 million bcm and 44 million tonnes a year to 2030 [F26, F27, F28]'. F27/F28 are the totals for the 1 April 2026-31 December 2030 term, not annual: the quote gives 239m bcm and 44 Mt for the contract, about 48m bcm and 9 Mt a year, which is what the symmetry justification correctly uses. Section 3 elsewhere gets this right ('quotes the volumes as the replacement term's gross').

The bear and base rows are numerically identical at Rp84.16 because the DCF floors at zero in both and the multiple leg is static in the engine, so 25% of the probability sits on a branch worth the same as base and the effective base mass is 85%. Section 5 discloses this explicitly ('that is an engine limitation, not a forecast') and states the target is if anything high, and the judge called the view neutral; but the scenario table itself should label the two rows as carrying the same value.

Section 1 reports 'net loss US$-127.6m' while the engine's np_parent line is US$-116.3m; the difference is the US$11.3m minority share of the FY2025 loss. Both are correct but a reader checking the model sees a mismatch.

fund record valuation.weights sums to 1.15 at file level (dcf 0.82 + ev 0.18 + pe 0.15 recorded at the default for the drop). The engine zeroes pe and drops it, so the effective pair is exactly 1.00 and the published Rp97.26 / -24.02% reproduces with no normaliser shave - the L1 artefact is gone. But the safety depends on pe staying dropped; a positive EPS would re-normalise the pair to 0.713/0.157.

flags.message: a.revenue_growth: bear -0.06 vs bull 0.04 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bear carries a fourth, one-sided revenue shock of -6pp a year because a contract loss is a disclosed, identified risk rather than the mirror of an upside: the top five customers are 78.0% of revenue [F26] and Adaro alone is 50.5 million bcm and 9.3 Mt a year to 31 December 2030 [F27, F28], after which it is a renewal, not backlog. The bull has no equivalent single-client upside because no award of that size is disclosed; the mirror of a lost contract would be an unsourced new contract, so the asymmetry is sourced on the downside only [S6 p.106, S4].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: The multiple weight is 18% against an industry default of 25%, and the 18% is the bull-branch probability of 15% corrected for the period alignment: the peer median is a trailing measure while the engine's multiple metric is the last audited year, and DOID's trailing EBITDA is higher than FY2025A by the 1H2026 improvement (US$69m against US$64m) [F21, F60, S3], which on a balance sheet where equity is a sixth of enterprise value lifts the cross-check's equity value by about a sixth. The engine divides by the last historical year and has no metric override, so carrying the leg at 15% x 1.17 = 18% is the same operation as applying the multiple to the trailing denominator. The weights sum to 1.00, so the effective multiple weight is 18% and the reverted-weight counterfactual (Rp96.3, -24.8%, still REDUCE) is stated once in section 4. P/E is carried at the industry-default 15% but contributes no weight: the company is loss-making (FY2025 parent loss US$116.3m on 7,357.2m shares [S2]) and the engine records it in dropped_methods. The DCF floors at zero in the base and bear, so the leg is the only positive value and the rating follows its weight; the report says so rather than claiming the operating case carries the call [S6, S2 p.32, F21].

news.title: Fitch Pangkas Rating BUMA dari A Jadi CCC-, Potensi Risiko Gagal Bayar Meningkat
news.note: Fitch cut BUMA's credit rating to CCC-(idn) from A, citing a liquidity crisis, maturing debt and higher default risk. BUMA is the mining contractor subsidiary of listed Delta Dunia Makmur.
